catalog_locator: Ch. 7 'Tone and Accent': tone statement at the chapter opening, p. 67; §7.2 'Accent System in Domung', pp. 71-74: the 'word-level accent' intuition-study sentence on p. 71; Table 31, the deciding statement and examples (60) on p. 72; shift examples (61), the 'closed syllables being heavier' sentence, the 'tentative' sentence and weight scale (62) on p. 73; non-finality examples (63), the exceptions sentences and the word-vs-phrase remark on p. 74; §7.3 acoustic figures (81% syllable-duration cue, fn. 20) on p. 76; restated in §8 Conclusion, p. 81.
catalog_quote: The results of the native speaker intuition study combined with acoustic analysis (see §7.3) provide sufficient evidence, despite the challenges mentioned above, to propose a bounded, quantity-sensitive, variable accent system for Domung. Specifically, accent falls within a bisyllabic window on the left edge of words with the first syllable as the preferred accent location as shown by (60). ... If the first (target) syllable within the accent window is lighter than the second syllable, then accent shifts to the second syllable as shown by (61) in accordance with the syllable weight scale detailed below in (62). ... This is also true in Domung with closed syllables being heavier than open syllables. ... I propose using this concept of a syllable weight scale for Domung with the scale shown in (62). The scale is tentative in nature, particularly with respect to the claim that syllable onset affects syllable weight as this is typologically unexpected and warrants further investigation. (62) Heaviest weight Closed syllable / contains long V or VV sequence: (C)VC / (C)VV(C) Open syllable with onset: CV Open syllable with no onset: V Lightest weight Open syllables with schwa nucleus: (C)ə ... Lastly, the final syllable of a word may not be accented; therefore, in bisyllabic words, accent is placed on the first syllable even if the first syllable is lighter than the second syllable as shown by (63).

new_statements.rule_in_words: No tone. Word accent falls in a two-syllable window at the left edge: on the first syllable by default, shifting to the second syllable when the second is heavier than the first on a four-level weight scale (closed or long-vowel/VV syllable > CV > onsetless V > syllable with schwa nucleus). Word-final syllables are never accented, so disyllables are always initial-accented. Main acoustic cue is syllable duration; pitch and intensity correlate poorly.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; only a single primary accent per word is analysed.
new_statements.exceptions: Author states the analysis 'accounts for the vast majority of the words within the corpus' but 'exceptions do exist' (p.74); the weight scale, especially onset contributing to weight, is called tentative; one of nine speakers perceived no accent at all; speaker-intuition agreement 88% on 14 test words.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent on isolated citation forms (14 nouns spoken in isolation by 3 speakers; corpus of 1600+ recorded words); relation between word-level and phrase-level stress explicitly left out of scope (p.74). Description is of the Buwa Me (central) dialect only (p.7).
new_statements.identity_note: Moe 2023 explicitly describes only the Buwa Me dialect of Domung (the central of three self-identified dialects in an east-west chain; fieldwork based around Bobongat village); language-level glottocode domu1246, ISO dev. No separate Glottolog dialect codes known to me for Domung dialects.

tone_statements.citation: Moe, Jonathan A. 2023. A Phonology of the Domung [dev] Language of Papua New Guinea with Acoustic Analysis. MA thesis, Trinity Western University. vii+119 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Domung does not exhibit lexical or grammatical tone, which is not surprising since no other Finisterre languages exhibit tone. A typological review of tone, and especially accent in Finisterre languages, is discussed in §7.1. The accent system of Domung is summarized in §7.2 along with a preliminary acoustic analysis of acoustic cues for accent in §7.3. … [p.81] While tone is not present in Domung nor in any other Finisterre languages, various and complex accent systems abound among these languages.
tone_statements.locator: p.67, §7 'Tone and Accent' opening paragraph; restated p.81, §8 Conclusion
tone_statements.summary: Not a tone language: no lexical or grammatical tone. Word accent in a two-syllable window at the left edge, weight-sensitive, cued mainly by syllable duration; pitch not a reliable accent cue.

sources.note: Ch.7 'Tone and Accent' (pp.67-79): no tone; a 'bounded, quantity-sensitive, variable accent system' -- accent in a two-syllable window at the left edge, first syllable preferred, shifts to the second syllable if that is heavier on a four-step weight scale ((C)VC/(C)VV(C) > CV > V > (C)ə); final syllables never accented, so disyllables are always initial-accented; native-speaker intuition test (8 speakers, 88% agreement) plus preliminary acoustics (syllable duration is the reliable cue; pitch/intensity poorly correlated); exceptions acknowledged.
